name: Merzouga Village Center
tagline: The compact heart of the desert village
description: The small central cluster of Merzouga, where guesthouses, shops, cafes, and tour operators gather near the road. It is walkable and practical, a place to arrange treks, grab supplies, and eat local tagine before heading out to the dunes that shimmer on the horizon.
bestFor: First-time visitors and easy access to services
pros: Easy to arrange treks and transport
cons: Less atmospheric than the dune edge

name: Erg Chebbi Dune-Edge Kasbahs
description: The string of kasbahs and desert lodges lining the western edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes, many toward Hassi Labied. This is the postcard Merzouga: rooms and camps that open straight onto towering orange sand, perfect for sunrise views, camel treks, and star-filled nights.
bestFor: Sunrise dune views and desert camps
pros: Wide range from simple to luxury camps

name: Hassi Labied
tagline: A quieter village at the dunes' edge
description: A small Berber village just north of Merzouga, sitting right against Erg Chebbi. It offers a calmer, more local base with palm groves, guesthouses, and easy dune access, popular with travelers who want the scenery without the busier central strip.
bestFor: A quieter, more authentic dune-edge stay

name: Khamlia
description: A small village a short drive south of Merzouga, known for its community of Gnaoua musicians of West African heritage. Visitors come to hear hypnotic live drumming and songs over mint tea, making it a cultural highlight rather than a lodging base.
